card.name: Helper verbs after a subject noun
card.fires_on: Small helper verbs such as can, may, be, has or the word the, right after a subject noun or verb. The strongest case is 'can' after 'oligohydramnios' in pregnancy warnings.

modes.label: Can/may after a condition
modes.description: Modal verb directly after a medical condition noun, before 'be associated' or 'not appear'.
modes.example: Resulting oligohydramnios<< can>> be associated with fetal lung hypoplas

modes.label: Other helper words
modes.description: Helper verb or 'the' in general web text, before a passive or noun phrase.
modes.example: He<< has>> served as a Director of the International Association

card.writes: The promoted and suppressed tokens suggest no clear link to the following word; the effect looks like it discourages 'reg' word forms.
card.plain: It fires on little helper words like 'can' or 'may' that come right after a subject, especially after a condition name.
